candidate_fix_policy.allowed: One bounded candidate for a simple diagnosed defect after preserving the first failure. Scope must be authorized by the active packet; writes outside allowlist are forbidden.
prohibited: kernel or launcher change in a draft-only packet
candidate_fix_policy.reviewer: Max for native correctness, lifetime, ABI, scheduler, unsafe or unclear semantics; independently reviewed candidate before any acceptance

completion: Draft each selected source/input specification and independent oracle within its exact allowlist; report unresolved semantics explicitly.
Represent every listed parameter without inflating logical case counts; feature-blocked execution still permits drafting.
No runtime execution, kernel/launcher edits, oracle weakening or invented capability acceptance in this draft-only packet.
Write the immutable packet-specific draft report, including exact changed-file hashes, unresolved oracles and any preserved failure/Max escalation.
After reporting, advance automatically only to the next packet already listed in the reviewed draft queue; request no repeated user permission and never enable execution.

reporting.failure_log_creation: Open a nonsymlink regular file with O_APPEND|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW, serialize one complete JSON object per line and fsync; never truncate, edit or remove old events.
reporting.failure_preservation: Immediately append the first unexpected failure event and preserve original output/source/diff/context before diagnosis; no hidden retry. Runtime/validation failures also retain the established root kernel.log record.
reporting.max_escalation: Record exact smallest reproducer, evidence paths and unresolved semantic question for Max. No model switch or production patch in a draft packet. Continue later independent drafting; mark dependency-blocked drafts precisely.
reporting.report_creation: Create once exclusively after draft work; do not replace a prior report. A resumed/revised run uses a new fresh_queue_run_id and links prior failed evidence.
reporting.scratch_write_exception: Only this packet report, original failure artifacts within its named failure directory, and append-only shared failure log. No production-source scope expansion.
